Title: DDNet: Dual-path Decoder Network for Occlusion Relationship Reasoning.

Abstract: Occlusion relationship reasoning based on CNNs consists of two subtasks: occlusion boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference. Due to essential differences between two subtasks in feature expression at higher/lower stages, challenging to carry on simultaneously in one network. Propose novel Dual-path Decoder Network, uniformly extracts occlusion info at higher stages and separates into two paths to recover boundary and orientation respectively in lower stages. Also new orthogonal representation for occlusion orientation and Orthogonal Orientation Regression loss. Multi-scale loss together with orientation regression loss guide boundary and orientation path learning. Experiments SOTA on PIOD and BSDS ownership.

Thesis: DDNet improves occlusion relationship reasoning by sharing high-stage occlusion features across two tasks and separating low-stage feature recovery into boundary and orientation paths, with orthogonal orientation representation and OOR loss and multi-scale supervision.

Position:
- Builds on CNN encoder-decoder occlusion relationship methods (DOOBNet, OFNet, DOC) and ResNet backbone; uses multi-scale supervision from HED/BDCN etc. Why? It adopts encoder-decoder and shared features, multi-scale supervision.
- Contrasts with previous unified decoder methods such as DOOBNet, OFNet that use entire decoder to extract shared info for both tasks; argues they ignore different effects of different level features and restrict learning flexibility. Also contrasts with continuous orientation regression (DOC, DOOBNet, OFNet) by using orthogonal vector representation/OOR loss.
- Critiques previous methods' representation/learning of occlusion orientation: regressing continuous orientation value difficult due to periodicity. Also previous multi-scale methods directly supervise backbone side-layer output lacking high-level guidance on lower stage recovery.
- Replicates? Maybe no replication. Could say "None explicitly; evaluates on same PIOD and BSDS ownership benchmarks used by prior work." Position "replicates" maybe benchmarks? It replicates evaluation datasets? Hmm.

Question/hypothesis: Can a dual-path decoder that shares high-stage occlusion information and separates low-stage spatial recovery for boundary and orientation improve occlusion relationship reasoning?
